questions.stem: A student adds 50 cm³ of hydrochloric acid to 50 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution in a polystyrene cup. The temperature rises from 21°C to 34°C. Why is a polystyrene cup used instead of a glass beaker?

options.text: Polystyrene is cheaper than glass
Polystyrene is a good insulator, reducing heat loss to surroundings so the temperature change is more accurate
Polystyrene does not react with acids
Polystyrene is transparent so you can see the reaction

questions.explanation: Polystyrene is an excellent thermal insulator. By minimising heat loss to the surroundings, the measured temperature change more accurately reflects the actual energy released by the reaction. A glass beaker would conduct heat away quickly, giving a smaller and less accurate temperature reading.

questions.stem: Self-heating coffee cans contain calcium oxide and water in separate compartments. When mixed, the temperature rises significantly. Which type of reaction is occurring and why?

options.text: Combustion - the calcium oxide burns in the water
Endothermic - the calcium oxide absorbs energy from the coffee
Exothermic - calcium oxide reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide, releasing heat
Neutralisation - the water neutralises the calcium oxide

questions.explanation: The reaction CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 is highly exothermic. The chemical energy stored in the reactants is greater than in the products, and the excess energy is released as heat to warm the coffee. This is not combustion (no burning) and not neutralisation (water is not an acid).

questions.stem: On an energy level diagram for an exothermic reaction, how are the reactants and products positioned?

options.text: Products are at a higher energy level than reactants
Products and reactants are at the same energy level
Reactants are at a higher energy level than products
The energy levels cannot be determined without specific data

questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, the reactants have more energy than the products. The energy difference is released to the surroundings. On an energy level diagram, the reactants line is drawn higher than the products line, with a downward arrow showing the energy released (negative enthalpy change).

questions.stem: A student measures the temperature change when magnesium is added to copper sulfate solution. The temperature rises by 15°C. She repeats the experiment using twice the volume of copper sulfate (same concentration) and twice the mass of magnesium. What would she expect?

options.text: The same temperature rise of 15°C
A temperature rise of 30°C
A temperature rise of about 15°C, since twice the energy heats twice the mass of solution
A temperature rise of 7.5°C

questions.explanation: Doubling the amounts of reactants releases twice the energy. However, there is also twice the volume of solution to heat. Since Q = mcDeltaT, doubling both Q and m means DeltaT stays approximately the same (about 15°C). The temperature change depends on the ratio of energy released to mass of solution heated.

questions.stem: Respiration in living cells is an exothermic process. What does this mean in terms of energy?

options.text: Cells absorb heat energy from their surroundings to function
Glucose gains energy when it is broken down
Energy is transferred from glucose to the surroundings, which cells use for life processes
Oxygen releases energy when it enters the cells

questions.explanation: Respiration (C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O) is exothermic because the products have less chemical energy than the reactants. The energy released is used by cells for muscle contraction, maintaining body temperature, building molecules, and other life processes. The energy comes from breaking and making chemical bonds.
